events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven by boat.** My expectation is a 3 (good).
- **Muskegon is the close second.** I'd expect a 3 there too, but its best boat report was for Chinook only.
- **South Haven and St. Joseph are a step behind.** I'd expect a 2 (average) at each.
- **Start around 100-140 ft of water, with lines 85-140 ft down** (Grand Haven's range). Use white or green flies on paddles or rotators, plus green spoons.
- **Check the wind before you launch.** The week before today had 12 mph average wind with gusts to 36 mph.

## Why

- **Grand Haven and Muskegon had the best boat reports.** The Sept 21 reports rated boats 3 (good) at both, with fish 85-140 ft down in 100-210 ft of water.
- **The buoy off Grand Haven and Muskegon dropped sharply.** The conditions summary for the week before today shows a 62 F buoy reading, down 21 F, which I'd expect means upwelling and cooler water near the shore.
- **South Haven and St. Joseph were only average.** Their Sept 21 boat reports were rated 2, with fish mostly on spoons.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is Sept 21, six days old)
- Grand Haven, Sept 21, boat: "Boat anglers were finding good numbers of immature salmon 85 to 140 feet down in 100 to 200 feet of water... White paddles with green or white flies worked very well along with green spoons." Quality 3.
- Grand Haven, Sept 21, pier: "Pier anglers found the salmon action to be slow." Quality 0.
- Muskegon, Sept 21, boat: "Boat anglers were finding immature Chinook salmon... 85 to 130 feet down in 130 to 210 feet of water... Rotators with white or green fly combinations worked well." Quality 3. A separate boat line said trolling near the breakwalls was "very slow" (quality 0).
- South Haven, Sept 21, boat: "The best water was beyond 120 feet... Most of these fish were caught on spoons." Quality 2.
- St. Joseph, Sept 21, boat: "The most productive water was around 120 feet." Quality 2.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Sept 14: boat quality 3 and 1. Spoons were the main lure at Grand Haven (55-110 ft down in 120-210 ft).

**Past seasons**
- The similarity search found no earlier seasons with water this cold near this date. The only matches were this September's own reports, at 70-73 F. So I have no historical base for this week's temperature.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool was in backtest mode, so these are a summary of the week before Sept 27, not live readings.
- Buoy surface water: Grand Haven and Muskegon 62 F (down 21 F, a possible upwelling). South Haven and St. Joseph 67 F (South Haven down 6 F).
- Satellite pier water: 68 F at all four ports, down 3-5 F in the last three days.
- Upwelling-favoring wind: 53-62 hours in the week at all four ports, with 21-37 hours in the last three days.
- Average wind 11-13 mph with gusts to 34-36 mph.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant): upwelling brings cold water and salmon toward shore, and mature Chinook in early fall tend to sit in water of 55 F or less.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old and the fall season moves fast, so treat these ratings as expectations, not current fishing.
- The water and wind figures come from a backtest summary, not live data. I have no live wind forecast for this weekend.
- The 62 F buoy reading is measured, but it is offshore. The cold-layer depth model was not available here, so I can't give a modeled depth.
- I don't have a Holland report. Holland's last report is from Sept 14, and this answer doesn't cover it.

## Sources

- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Sept 21 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32e369d
- South Haven and St. Joseph, Sept 21 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32e369d
- Earlier context, Sept 14 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32cff90
